comparator.academicYear: 2025-2026 (Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences course descriptions, the latest edition listed on the programme page; programme pages checked 2026-09-30)
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official Maastricht University programme page 'Courses & curriculum' (s0), which describes the three-year programme (year 1: public health, determinants and the EU, diseases, environment and health technology, research methods and statistics; year 2: demography, ageing and migration, lifestyle, work and health, the Krakow excursion and quantitative methods, then a free-choice minor semester; year 3: health systems, EU health policy, and a placement with thesis), and from the Faculty of Health, Medicine and Life Sciences 2025-2026 course descriptions (s3), which list every course with its code, period and EC: year 1 totals 60 EC (EPH1021 9, EPH1022 9, EPH1024 9, EPH1025 9, EPH1027 6, EPH1026 5, EPH1226 1 and eight competency-line modules of 2 EC), year 2 totals 30 EC without the minor, and year 3 totals 60 EC including the 30-EC Placement and Thesis (EPH3025). The 30-EC minor is not listed as a course: the page says students 'take a semester on a subject of your choice (the minor period)', and its 30 EC is derived by arithmetic (180 less 60, 30 and 60 EC), so it is kept as one explicit open component rather than filled with named courses. The Specialized Competency Lines (epidemiology, methodology, policy advocacy and statistics; philosophy of public health) are separately credited 1-2 EC modules and are listed individually. The programme page names no formal route or specialisation for the Bachelor European Public Health. The 2025-2026 course descriptions are the latest edition published on the programme page; the official curriculum page itself gives only narrative descriptions and example courses without EC values. A human may wish to confirm the 30-EC minor against the current Education and Examination Regulations.

courses: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory

core: Public health foundations, determinants and epidemiology: Health, Health Determinants and the European Union, and Demography and Epidemiology of Ageing and Migration, which teach the concepts of health and public health, determinants and socio-economic health inequalities, demography and epidemiological methods applied to population ageing

Disease and health technology: Communicable and Non-communicable Diseases in the EU and WHO-Euro (infectious disease, antimicrobial resistance, cardiovascular disease, diabetes, cancer, mental health) and Health-Technological Innovation and EU Competencies (pharmaceuticals, medical devices, big data)

European Union institutions, law, politics and health policy: the EU treaties, institutions and decision-making taught in year 1, and Health Policies at EU Level and Global Health Europe, which teaches health policy making, actors, advocacy and evidence-informed policy in a multilevel EU setting

Comparing European health systems: (Public) Health Care Systems in the EU, which analyses and compares the organisation, financing, insurance, reform and governance of health systems through health-system frameworks

Research methods, statistics and evidence: the interwoven Specialized Competency Lines (epidemiology, research methodology, statistics), Introduction to Statistical Methods for Data Analysis, Introduction to Quantitative Research Methods (programme evaluation) and the Year 1 literature-review paper, covering qualitative and quantitative methods and critical use of evidence
Ethics and philosophy of public health: the ethical issues and dilemmas of public health in Europe in year 1 and the Philosophy of Public Health competency line across the three years
Independent research and thesis: the Thesis Proposal and the 30-EC Placement and Thesis, in which students conduct independent research on a public-health question
adjacent: Social and behavioural determinants of health: social determinants of health and disease, lifestyle (diet, exercise, tobacco) and work as determinants, health promotion and psychological perspectives, studied through a socio-ecological model in Lifestyle, Work and Health in the EU

Health communication and policy advocacy: the Policy Advocacy competency line, which teaches students to understand, critique and influence public policy, and the programme's aim to develop skills in communication and policy advocacy

Environment, climate and sustainable health: the environment as a determinant of health (climate change, air and water quality, biodiversity, food supply) and sustainability in Healthy Environments and Sustainability in the EU
questions: How can European countries and the EU jointly address cross-border public-health threats such as pandemics, climate change, health inequities and ageing populations?
How do health systems, policies and outcomes compare across European countries?

unpacks consumer behaviour, engagement and trust-building in marketing strategy; it makes a specific complementary contribution to behaviour change and the design of health-promotion and advocacy messages, but it is not a health-marketing course

teaches research design, sampling and descriptive and inferential statistics (central tendency, spread, association, univariate and bivariate tests and analysis of variance); it directly implements the target's introductory statistics and research-methodology training and is the formal prerequisite of Public Economics

examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics within organisations; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the work and workplace dimension of the target's Lifestyle, Work and Health in the EU, without covering occupational health

develops data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation and an own data-analysis research project; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the target's work with real-world health data in its statistics and quantitative-methods modules

examines how sustainability policies are made and enforced, which actors shape them and what makes policy effective; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the sustainable-policy and governance questions of the target's Healthy Environments and Sustainability in the EU, without health content

covers the drivers and impacts of climate change, including effects on food production, health and migration, and climate governance and justice; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the climate-and-health strand of the target's Healthy Environments and Sustainability in the EU, but treats health only as one of several impacts

teaches the analytical tools for comparing political systems with theory-driven qualitative and quantitative research; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the comparative approach of the target's health-systems and policy modules, without covering health systems

teaches drug origin, pharmacokinetics, therapeutic use and toxicity and the principles of rational drug development; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the pharmaceutical strand of the target's Health-Technological Innovation and EU Competencies, without the regulatory, policy or medical-device content

examines the bio-psycho-social approach to health and illness, health psychology theories and behaviour-related interventions in medical settings; it directly implements the health-behaviour and psychological-determinants content of the target's Lifestyle, Work and Health in the EU, without the European policy or occupational-health dimension

teaches persuasion strategies, framing, nudging and the ethics of persuasion, including sustainability and science messaging; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the communication and advocacy skills the target develops, without any health content

alternatives.label: Closest match to European Public Health: Epidemiology, Disease, Psychology and Research Methods with EU Law, Politics and Sustainability
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has five epidemiology and biomedical courses (Epidemiology & Public Health, Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, Infection & Immunity, Mechanisms of Disease and Pharmacology), five psychology and research-methods courses (Introduction to Brain & Behavior, Medical & Health Psychology, Statistics & Experimental Methods, Advanced Research Seminar, Lifespan Developmental Psychology), four law and politics courses on the EU and comparative systems (Law, Society & Justice, Foundations of European Union Law, European Union Politics, Foundations of Comparative Politics), two sociology courses, Research Methods & Statistics, Introduction to Data Science, Ethics, Public Economics, Persuasive Communication, two sustainability courses and Personal & Professional Development. The label names the epidemiology, disease, psychology and research-methods core together with the EU law, politics and sustainability strands without presenting any single strand as the whole programme.
alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response to the Bachelor European Public Health at Maastricht University, whose curriculum combines public health foundations and epidemiology, communicable and non-communicable disease, health technology, European Union institutions and health policy, the comparison of European health systems, social and environmental determinants, a research-methods and statistics line and a thesis. UCR offers no health-policy, health-systems or environmental-health course, so the programme builds on its public-health epidemiology course and its biomedical and health-psychology courses, adds EU law and politics and comparative politics for the European dimension, and uses economics, sustainability governance, ethics and communication courses as specific complementary contributions; they do not replace the dedicated European public-health, health-systems and health-law training that UCR does not offer.
progression: Every formal prerequisite is scheduled in an earlier semester: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine and Brain & Behavior in semester 1 precede Infection & Immunity, Medical & Health Psychology, Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Advanced Research Seminar and Lifespan Developmental Psychology; Law, Society & Justice in semester 1 precedes Foundations of European Union Law; Research Methods & Statistics in semester 2 precedes Public Economics. Epidemiology & Public Health, the two introductory research-methods courses and the sociology and law introductions come first; the statistics-heavy Statistics & Experimental Methods follows Research Methods & Statistics, Persuasive Communication and the comparative and EU politics courses are placed after the introductory social-science courses, and the Advanced Research Seminar is placed in the final semester as the research-preparation capstone.

alternatives.label: Health Behaviour, Psychology and Communication: Social Determinants, Mental Health and Public Advocacy
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum has eight psychology and cognition courses (Brain & Behavior, Social Psychology, Medical & Health Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Higher Order Functions, Statistics & Experimental Methods and Advanced Research Seminar), three communication and rhetoric courses, four sociology courses (including Qualitative Research Methodology), three behavioural, organisational and marketing courses, Epidemiology & Public Health, Research Methods & Statistics, Ethics, Data Science, European Union Politics and Personal & Professional Development. The label names the behavioural, psychological and communication focus and its social-determinants and advocacy application, and does not claim the epidemiology, health-policy or biomedical coverage of the closest match.
alternatives.concept: The target's own social and behavioural strand, developed as a programme: the social and psychological determinants of health, lifestyle and work as determinants, mental health, and health communication and public-health advocacy. UCR has no health-promotion, health-communication or public-health course beyond Epidemiology & Public Health, so the programme combines UCR's health, social and cognitive psychology, sociology, behavioural economics, organisational psychology and rhetoric and persuasion courses with Epidemiology & Public Health and the methods courses as specific complementary contributions; they do not replace dedicated health-promotion or health-communication training.
alternatives.distinctness: Alternative 1 organises the programme around the target's core: epidemiology, disease, EU law and politics, health systems and sustainability. Alternative 2 changes the organising priority to the target's social and behavioural strand, following the direct programme interests in the social and psychological determinants of health (5846), health communication and media (5843) and public-health advocacy (5856) and the target's Lifestyle, Work and Health module and Policy Advocacy competency line. It drops ten Alternative 1 courses (Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, Law, Society & Justice, Infection & Immunity, Pharmacology, Mechanisms of Disease, Foundations of European Union Law, Public Economics, Climate Change, Foundations of Comparative Politics and Governance of Sustainability) and adds ten courses that Alternative 1 does not contain: Social Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Higher Order Functions, Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Behavioral Economics, Marketing & Consumer Engagement, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, The Art of Rhetorical Communication and Rhetoric in Action. The two programmes share 14 courses, including the epidemiology, methods and health-psychology courses, and the 10 different courses follow directly from the change in organising priority.

progression: Brain & Behavior and Epidemiology & Public Health in semester 1 precede Medical & Health Psychology, Abnormal Psychology, Lifespan Developmental Psychology, Higher Order Functions and the Advanced Research Seminar, which all require Brain & Behavior. Research Methods & Statistics in semester 2 precedes Psychology of Organizations & Leadership, Marketing & Consumer Engagement and Behavioral Economics, which require it. The Art of Rhetorical Communication in semester 1 precedes Persuasive Communication in semester 3 and Rhetoric in Action in semester 6, Social Psychology comes before the later psychology courses that build on it, and the Advanced Research Seminar is placed last.

selection.assessment: Two UCR alternatives are defensible and production stopped at two. Alternative 1 owns thirteen generator-eligible rows that describe the target's own core (5833 and 5834 on European and cross-border public health; 5835 on ageing populations; 5836 on cross-border epidemics and infectious disease; 5838 to 5841 on health systems, EU health policy, the politics of public health and public-health law; 5845 on ethics; 5849 and 5850 on qualitative research and statistics and health-data analysis; 5854 on comparing healthcare systems; and 5859 on independent research). Alternative 2 is built on the direct programme interests in the social and psychological determinants of health (5846), health communication and media (5843) and public-health advocacy (5856), which form one coherent behavioural and communicative direction corroborated by the target's Lifestyle, Work and Health module and Policy Advocacy competency line; it supplies ten different courses and shares 14 with Alternative 1, so it passes the 30 EC / 4 course floor in both directions. Three further candidate directions cannot be built into a third valid and coherent UCR programme. Climate, environment and sustainable health (5837 and 5847) is supported by the target's Healthy Environments and Sustainability in the EU module, but UCR has no environmental-health, toxicology or exposure course, so a programme would consist of environmental-science courses with one epidemiology course and would not implement a health concept; the two sustainability courses it would rely on already serve Alternative 1 as complementary contributions. Healthcare management (5842) has no UCR counterpart: the available management, business and economics courses sit behind business gateway courses and contain no health-care content, so the differing courses would be an assortment. Field placement in a health organisation (5858) concerns a work placement, and UCR has no placement course in the enriched course database (the standardized optional independent research element is a comparison-only element, not a course), so no 24-course programme can implement it.

blocks: Epidemiology, research methods, statistics and evidence

Epidemiology & Public Health teaches epidemiology as the science of studying disease, risk and change over time and of evaluating evidence, the core of Demography and Epidemiology of Ageing and Migration (epidemiological concepts and methods, research designs, association measures, bias and causal interpretation); it lacks the demography, ageing and migration topics and the EU focus.

Research Methods & Statistics covers descriptive and inferential statistics (central tendency, spread, association, univariate and bivariate tests), the subject of Introduction to Statistical Methods for Data Analysis; it is broader on research design and does not use health data.

Statistics & Experimental Methods covers multivariate models (regression, logistic regression, ANOVA) and experimental design, the statistical-analysis and study-design part of Introduction to Quantitative Research Methods (chi-square tests, t-tests, regression and trial designs); it does not cover programme evaluation or process evaluation.

Advanced Research Seminar teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis for evidence-based policy, the evidence-synthesis skill at the centre of the Year 1 literature-review paper (finding, interpreting and combining public-health evidence); it is a statistical synthesis course and does not teach academic writing.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Thesis Proposal is writing the research proposal for the bachelor thesis under supervision; UCR has no course for preparing an own thesis proposal, and Advanced Research Seminar is aligned with the literature-review component, so the relationship would be generic research training.

Infection & Immunity covers host-pathogen interaction, microbial resistance strategies and the immune response, the infectious-disease half of Communicable and Non-communicable Diseases in the EU and WHO-Euro; it does not cover its policy frames, non-communicable diseases or epidemiology.

Pharmacology covers drug origin, therapeutic use, toxicity and rational drug development, the pharmaceutical innovation strand of Health-Technological Innovation and EU Competencies; it does not cover medical devices, big data, safety assessment or the EU regulatory competencies.
Behaviour, psychology and social determinants of health

Medical & Health Psychology covers the bio-psycho-social approach to health and illness, health-psychology theory and interventions, matching the individual health-behaviour and intervention content of Lifestyle, Work and Health in the EU; it does not cover work characteristics or EU lifestyle and occupational-health policy.
European Union law, politics, economics and health systems

Foundations of European Union Law covers the EU institutional framework, legal order, fundamental rights and internal market, matching the EU history, treaties, institutions and legal-structures part of Health, Health Determinants and the European Union; it does not cover the concepts of health and public health, health determinants and health inequalities, which make up most of the component.

European Union Politics covers EU actors, institutions, decision-making rules and how interests are turned into policy, matching the multilevel EU policy-making, actors and advocacy of Health Policies at EU Level and Global Health Europe; it has no health-policy content or global-health dimension.

Public Economics covers market failure, public goods, externalities, taxation, public spending and redistribution, matching the financing and market part of (Public) Health Care Systems in the EU; it does not cover health-system frameworks, insurance schemes or health-system reforms.

Climate Change covers the drivers and societal impacts of climate change, including effects on health, food and migration, matching the climate-change part of Healthy Environments and Sustainability in the EU; it does not cover air and water quality, built environments or the health-environment policy focus.

Excursion, year 2 paper, minor and placement with thesis
Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the 1-EC excursion to Kraków is a field visit to the Polish health-care system; UCR has no comparable field-visit course among the scheduled courses.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the Year 2 Paper is an individual assignment on one of the four main content modules; no scheduled UCR course is a counterpart to this programme-specific paper.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the 30-EC minor is a semester of free choice, including study abroad, which is open elective space without defined content; it is retained as explicit open space rather than matched to any UCR course.

notes.text: The Bachelor European Public Health combines public health epidemiology, health policy and law in the European Union, health systems and health technology with a programme-wide methods line and a placement with thesis. At UCR, students can approach public health through fields such as epidemiology, biomedicine, health psychology, sociology, EU law and politics and sustainability. These programmes therefore offer related perspectives rather than reproducing a full public health curriculum.

The Bachelor European Public Health includes a more extensive sequence in European health policy, health systems and health law, environmental health and health technology. At UCR, students can study epidemiology, disease, EU law and politics and sustainability, but UCR does not offer the same depth or sequence in public health.
